summary: Ephemeral proxy surge in eu-west caused runtime KV-cache eviction race and elevated 502s for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
NimbleDocs (dedicated tenant) observed a rapid increase in 502/504 responses from the API gateway for requests routed to their eu-west capacity pool starting 2026-03-12 08:40 UTC. Error rate peaked ~12% of requests for ~18 minutes and caused user-facing timeouts in their ingestion pipeline.

Impact:
- Customer ingestion jobs for embeddings failed intermittently (502/504) causing backoff/retry storms on their side.
- End-users reported degraded UX for search indexing.
- No billing discrepancy reported; primary impact is availability.

Environment:
- prod - eu-west (dedicated capacity pool for NimbleDocs)
- Tenant uses large embedding batches (up to 10k vectors) and long text prompts.

Steps to reproduce (observed with customer test payloads):
1) Upload 10k vector embedding batch via /v1/embeddings concurrently from 5 pods with 10 parallel connections each.
2) Observe API gateway latency climb and intermittent 502/504s.
3) Check runtime logs for KV-cache eviction warnings and OOM-ish stack traces.

Observed behavior / logs:
- API gateway logs: repeated upstream-reset/502 with message "upstream reset while reading response" and 502s correlated with high accept-queue length.
- Serving runtime stderr: repeated warnings "kvcache: shard eviction contention" followed by a few processes exiting with SIGABRT around 08:42 UTC.
- Node metrics: GPU utilization remained moderate (~45-60%) but host CPU and io-wait spiked on the runtime pods during the event.
- Autoscaler: no scale-up events triggered during the 18-minute window due to hysteresis settings.

Investigation notes:
- Timeline reconstructed from logs and metrics (support timeline attached): ingress surge at 08:40, first runtime eviction warning 08:41, proxy queue growth and gateway 502 spike 08:42, short runtime process exits 08:42–08:44, gradual recovery by 09:00 after customer retried with lower concurrency.
- Hypothesis 1: Ephemeral proxy (fronting envoy instances) experienced a surge of ephemeral connections from the tenant's worker fleet; accept-queue/backpressure spilled into runtime proxy and amplified KV-cache eviction races in the runtime.
- Hypothesis 2: Runtime's KV-cache eviction path had a contention window where concurrent prefetch/evict operations could block main request threads, increasing latency and causing upstream timeouts. Under moderate GPU usage but high host CPU/io pressure, this surface triggered process watchdogs.
- Reproduction attempts in staging using scaled-down tenant config produced similar KV eviction warnings when we simulated identical concurrency and batch sizes.
- No immediate evidence of model-level OOM; process exits appear to be watchdog/crash on blocked main loop rather than native GPU OOMs.

Relevant traces and links:
- API gateway SLO dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/dashboards/apigw-euwest
- Serving runtime logs (snippet): https://logs.redwood.internal/?q=SUP-763821
- Slack incident channel: #support-sup-763821 (customer channel: nimbledocs-support)
comments: 2026-03-12 09:02 - Alex Chen (Support): Initial triage complete. Reached out to SRE to check proxy accept queues and runtime eviction metrics. Added customer to incident channel.

2026-03-12 09:15 - SRE - Michael O'Neil: Observed accept queue bursts on fronting proxies correlated with 08:40-08:44. No underlying host OOM reported. CPU sys/io spike on runtime host. Working hypothesis: blocking kvcache eviction causing request stalls.

2026-03-12 10:00 - Support - Priya Rao: Customer confirmed they deployed a bursty batch job at 08:35 UTC that aligns with our window. They temporarily reduced concurrency which returned service to normal.

2026-03-12 13:30 - Eng - Sara Gomez: Reproduced KV eviction contention in staging. Added instrumentation PR to add per-shard eviction backoff and metrics (see PR #4821). Will run canary on a small subset of replicas.

2026-03-13 10:45 - Alex Chen: Applied temporary mitigations for NimbleDocs: tenant-level soft concurrency cap at the API gateway and recommended batch-size limit of 2k vectors per request. Customer applied immediately and reported improved stability.
2026-03-14 08:20 - Priya Rao: Customer acceptance testing in progress. Awaiting canary results from Eng and confirmation that autoscaler hysteresis settings are adjusted for burst detection.

2026-03-14 12:01 - Eng - Luis Martinez: Canary patch deployed to 3/24 replicas in eu-west; initial telemetry shows reduced eviction contention and lower proxy queue depth during synthetic burst tests. Planning wider rollout after one more verification run.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: tenant-level soft concurrency caps at API gateway and recommended batch-size limit implemented by customer, reducing occurrence to near-zero for now. Engineering opened PR github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 to add per-shard eviction backoff and new kvcache contention metrics. Autoscaler config review ticket INT-4420 created to tune hysteresis for dedicated pools. Next steps: complete runtime PR rollout (wider canary then full roll), update tenant guidance for large embedding batches, and consider short-term adjustment to autoscaler thresholds. Permanent fix ETA: 2026-03-20 pending full rollout and post-canary verification.
